decision_reason: The French public-sector design-system team publishes a documented, independently installable React implementation; DINUM material describes reuse by multiple beta.gouv.fr services. Public source, MIT terms and the earliest defensible licensed-source year are directly evidenced.

government_provenance.note: DINUM's BlueHats project page identifies the React DSFR project and its public-sector maintainer.

public_source.note: Canonical public repository contains the React implementation and installation/documentation material.

eligible_license.note: The repository LICENSE grants MIT terms; its first license-bearing source commit is dated 2022-09-20 (https://github.com/codegouvfr/react-dsfr/commit/e75a5445eba49d5d08fe6ef87f54bad436557d55).

primary_evidence.note: DINUM reports that React DSFR is reused by multiple beta.gouv.fr incubator services, supporting the documented-reuse notability pathway.

agency: DINUM, Pôle Open Source et Communs Numériques (BlueHats)
family_note: React implementation of the French State Design System (DSFR), distinct from the base DSFR design-system product.

decision_reason: The Federal Statistical Office's national I14Y metadata platform is documented as a production catalogue of public-sector datasets and APIs, with its code now publicly released under MIT. The current public licensed source appears in 2026; the older platform production date is not used as the open-source year.

government_provenance.note: The Federal Statistical Office's own publication identifies I14Y as a federal metadata platform developed by the FSO (with FOITT).

public_source.note: The canonical repository is public and contains the platform source and project documentation.

eligible_license.note: The repository LICENSE grants MIT terms; the first license-bearing source commit is dated 2026-09-09 (https://github.com/metadata-swiss/I14Y/commit/9dacc8be8b1aa1005459cb02b07a811919a00332).

primary_evidence.note: The project's official handbook announces public GitHub source publication; the FSO publication documents the production national metadata service.

agency: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO), with the Federal Office of Information Technology, Systems and Telecommunication (FOITT)
status_note: The service has operated since 2021; code availability is newly evidenced in 2026 and is the year recorded here.

decision_reason: Vitam is a French interministerial digital-archiving software program with public release and deployment documentation. The repository grants CeCILL 2.1; 2017 is the earliest defensible public licensed-code year evidenced by its license history and GitHub release record.

government_provenance.note: The official Programme Vitam page describes the French government's interministerial open-source digital-archiving program and its software releases.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the archival platform source, documentation and release history.

eligible_license.note: The source license is CeCILL 2.1; its first license-bearing commit is dated 2017-01-13 (https://github.com/ProgrammeVitam/vitam/commit/174fc39bd731d5a63daa909a6c04863d8e598231).

primary_evidence.note: The program's official presentation identifies the archival product, its interministerial government sponsorship, deployments and public release channel.

family_note: Review this repository as the core archival platform, not as a separate deployment instance or adjacent Vitam interface.

decision_reason: The Federal Archives identify SIARD Suite as their database-archiving software and the current public repository carries CDDL terms, but the first public licensed-code year is not settled: the product dates to 2007 and a 2009 bespoke license agreement exists, while the current GitHub history begins in 2022. Hold rather than equate product age with public open-source availability.

government_provenance.note: The Swiss Federal Archives' product page says it developed SIARD Suite for archiving relational databases.

public_source.note: The canonical GitHub repository is public and contains source code and release documentation.

eligible_license.note: The repository carries the CDDL-1.0 license; the first license-file commit in this GitHub history is dated 2022-09-14 (https://github.com/sfa-siard/siard-suite/commit/d4150338825e83a75895228b686a68e0dd2220ad).

primary_evidence.note: Official manual says Suite 1.0 was developed in 2007 and published under CDDL, but the source does not date that public licensed-code release; a 2009 official agreement is not itself proof of CDDL availability.

metadata_note: Potential first-source year requires archival evidence of when CDDL-licensed source became publicly available; do not substitute Suite 1.0's development year.

decision_reason: The Fabrique des ministères sociaux publishes DashLord as a reusable web-quality dashboard with setup guidance; its official site demonstrates dashboard use across public-sector services. The Apache-2.0 source is public and the earliest defensible licensed-source year is 2021.

government_provenance.note: The project's official about page says DashLord originated at the Fabrique des ministères sociaux and describes its government web-quality purpose.

public_source.note: Canonical public source includes the dashboard implementation, configuration and reuse guidance.

eligible_license.note: The repository license grants Apache-2.0 terms; the first LICENSE commit is dated 2021-09-03 (https://github.com/SocialGouv/dashlord/commit/035a55640235b98bbf6f08878673c63421faf7af).

primary_evidence.note: The maintained live dashboard provides actual ministry and beta.gouv.fr service dashboards; project documentation explains how to deploy a reusable instance.

agency: Fabrique des ministères sociaux (French Ministry of Social Affairs digital factory)
family_note: Count the reusable dashboard software as one product, not each configured dashboard or scanned service as a separate product.

decision_reason: The Swiss e-ID program distributes the Generic Issuer as a reusable trust-infrastructure component with a deployment cookbook. The public repository grants MIT terms; 2025 is supported by the first license-bearing source commit.

government_provenance.note: The official swiyu-admin-ch organization identifies itself as the swiyu Swiss Trust Infrastructure public-beta program and links to federal e-ID material.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the Generic Issuer implementation and deployment/readme material.

eligible_license.note: The source LICENSE grants MIT terms; its first license-bearing commit is dated 2025-08-12 (https://github.com/swiyu-admin-ch/swiyu-issuer/commit/22e2fb9870baf605d2a32deeead6f4139468e24e).

primary_evidence.note: The official technical cookbook gives step-by-step deployment instructions and explains that each issuer operates its own Generic Issuer instance.

agency: Swiss Federal Office of Justice (FOJ), Swiss Confederation e-ID / swiyu program
family_note: A reusable issuer component of swiyu Trust Infrastructure; treat wallet, issuer and verifier siblings as a product-family decision, not one repo per deployed issuer.

decision_reason: GDS maintains accessible-autocomplete as a standalone, npm-installable JavaScript package with implementation, examples and installation guidance. This is an independently distributed accessibility component rather than a documentation/example-only repository; the MIT grant and first licensed source year are directly evidenced.

government_provenance.note: The package metadata identifies Government Digital Service as author; the repository README says the GOV.UK Design System team maintains it.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the library source, built package, tests and usage examples.

eligible_license.note: The source license is MIT; its first LICENSE.txt commit is dated 2017-01-19 (https://github.com/alphagov/accessible-autocomplete/commit/84bc245e7fa28a1e796d7f913bb5f733c3b3253b).

primary_evidence.note: The GDS-maintained README documents a standalone npm installation and accessible-autocomplete API; the package is an agency-distributed reusable component.

agency: Government Digital Service (GDS), GOV.UK Design System team
family_note: A standalone npm package maintained by the GOV.UK Design System team; do not duplicate the GOV.UK Design System or treat its examples as separate products.

decision_reason: FIRe is the Spanish public-administration electronic-signature integration system, officially documented for public bodies and published with installation/integration material. Upstream states GPL 2+ and EUPL 1.1; 2017 is the earliest defensible publicly licensed source year. Some optional cloud-signature connectors require private dependencies, which the upstream README discloses.

government_provenance.note: The current FIRe security-update notice (13 March 2026) is issued by the Centro de Servicios de la AEAD and identifies the Agencia Estatal de Administración Digital under the Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Service. The legacy CTT FIRe ficha still names SGAD; BOE RD 1125/2024 states AEAD replaces SGAD (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2024-22935).

public_source.note: The public repository contains the server, clients, build files and integration architecture; the README identifies private optional connector dependencies separately.

eligible_license.note: LICENSE/LICENSE.txt names GNU GPL version 2.0 and EUPL version 1.1 and supplies both license texts; README says GPL 2+ and EUPL 1.1. The PHP client header expressly permits GPL v2-or-later OR EUPL v1.1-or-later (https://github.com/ctt-gob-es/fire/blob/master/fire-client-php/fire_api.php). The license field records both upstream-stated licenses without asserting a conjunctive SPDX expression or broader repo-wide OR. First LICENSE commit is 2017-10-13 (https://github.com/ctt-gob-es/fire/commit/901396fc50bd98a733038117e6432d635743aab9).

primary_evidence.note: CTT publishes the source link, downloadable integration kit, deployment/integration documentation, and a legal notice that separately says EUPL 1.1 or later for the solution.

agency: Agencia Estatal de Administración Digital (AEAD), Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública
metadata_note: Upstream documents some optional cloud-signature connectors as dependent on private, separately licensed libraries; the public core/source and other integration modules remain available under the stated grants. Current AEAD attribution is supported by the March 2026 FIRe notice and the BOE succession rule; the static CTT ficha is legacy.
agency_note: Current FIRe operational support and update notices identify AEAD; the legacy CTT solution ficha retains historical SGAD attribution. AEAD succeeded SGAD upon effective constitution under RD 1118/2024.

decision_reason: Démarches Simplifiées / Démarche numérique is a live DINUM-run platform used by public bodies to create and process online administrative procedures; its official CGU link the AGPL source and document platform administration. The first license-bearing source history supports 2017.

government_provenance.note: DINUM's official CGU identify it as the service operator and general platform administrator and link the code source.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the platform source; the previous beta.gouv repository identity redirects to this project lineage.

eligible_license.note: The repository license is AGPL-3.0; the first license-bearing commit is dated 2017-04-03 (https://github.com/demarche-numerique/demarche.numerique.gouv.fr/commit/6deb4169e8cacbec1ca336ab86989a5ff20de64d).

primary_evidence.note: DINUM describes the production platform, its public-sector availability and integrations; its documentation provides operational CGU and user guidance.

product_identity: Démarches Simplifiées / Démarche numérique administrative-procedure platform
family_note: Current repository is the canonical continuation of the former demarches-simplifiees.fr codebase; do not double-count the renamed service/repository.

decision_reason: The Department for Education's live Register trainee teachers service and provider guidance establish an operational national service; the repository README identifies the service and production domain. The public code carries MIT terms, first evidenced in 2020.

government_provenance.note: DfE's official guidance identifies the Register trainee teachers service and its use by teacher-training providers in England.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the service source; its README names DfE and the production register-trainee-teachers.service.gov.uk service.

eligible_license.note: The repository LICENCE grants MIT terms; the initial licensed application commit is dated 2020-08-13 (https://github.com/DFE-Digital/register-trainee-teachers/commit/5727e3ca1a22195be31c13c996d5c95129ceb0ca).

primary_evidence.note: DfE documentation says the service replaced the Database of Trainee Teachers and is used to register trainees, record outcomes and check funding.

decision_reason: The source is publicly licensed and attributable to the UK Government Incubator for AI, but the evidence reviewed only establishes an early-stage validator repository and demo/evaluation tooling; no production government service, stable release, or documented independent reuse was found. Hold pending a stronger maturity/notability pathway.

government_provenance.note: The i.AI organization states it is a GDS team within DSIT and lists Planning Drawing Validator among its projects.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the source, README and local build/deployment instructions.

eligible_license.note: The source LICENSE is MIT; its first license-bearing commit is dated 2025-11-28 (https://github.com/i-dot-ai/planning-drawing-validator/commit/de1dc830d47da7302fb71000fe440f9f33a55955).

primary_evidence.note: The repo identifies the prototype's function and author but provides no public evidence reviewed here of production deployment or independent adoption.

agency: Incubator for Artificial Intelligence (i.AI), Government Digital Service, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
status_note: No stable release, production deployment or documented reuse identified in this review.

decision_reason: Sites Conformes is an agency-distributed CMS for creating official .gouv.fr sites, based on Wagtail and the French State Design System. Its public repository includes architecture and deployment material under AGPL-3.0; 2023 is supported by the initial licensed source history.

government_provenance.note: The numerique-gouv organization is the French government's DINUM digital-services organization; this repository's README describes the state-sites CMS.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the CMS, deployment configuration, documentation and publiccode metadata.

eligible_license.note: The LICENSE is AGPL-3.0; the first license-bearing source commit is dated 2023-01-10 (https://github.com/numerique-gouv/sites-conformes/commit/006c0aec2ff943adb21afa960a29cc83b1de462d).

primary_evidence.note: The official Sites beta.gouv.fr portal and project repository document the CMS for building public .gouv.fr sites and provide architecture/deployment guidance.

family_note: Sites Conformes is the renamed continuation of Sites Faciles; do not count the former name as a separate product.

decision_reason: The ONS Design System is an actively released, npm-installable design system with official ONS service-manual guidance for installation, components, prototyping and use in ONS services. Its public repository grants MIT terms; 2018 is supported by the first license commit.

government_provenance.note: ONS publishes and maintains the design-system guidance in its official service manual; the repo README points consumers to that manual.

public_source.note: The ONSdigital repository is public and includes reusable design-system source and release instructions.

eligible_license.note: The repository LICENSE grants MIT terms; the first LICENSE commit is dated 2018-12-21 (https://github.com/ONSdigital/design-system/commit/3b9fa52cfbca27b64d14e699922b6ad40cd48846).

primary_evidence.note: ONS documents how to install the package and use its components/templates; each release is published as @ons/design-system.

agency: Office for National Statistics (ONS), Design System team
family_note: ONS-specific design system, distinct from GOV.UK Design System.
